data.sop_name: Search and Seizure under the NDPS Act
data.objective: To ensure lawful search, seizure, sampling, storage and reporting of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in accordance with the NDPS Act, 1985 and associated rules.

legal_basis.purpose: Power to issue warrants and authorizations.
Search, seizure and arrest based on prior information in buildings, conveyances or enclosed places.
Search and seizure in public places.
Power to stop and search conveyances.
Conditions for personal search.
Disposal and reporting after arrest and seizure.
Disposal, inventory, photography and sampling of seized narcotic drugs.
Safe custody of seized articles.
Reporting of arrest and seizure to superior officers.

procedure.title: Record Intelligence
procedure.description: Record information received regarding narcotic offences as required under Section 42 before initiating action where applicable.

procedure.title: Obtain Authorization
procedure.description: Obtain warrant or authorization under Section 41 whenever required. Emergency searches shall follow provisions of Section 42.

procedure.title: Identify Search Location
procedure.description: Determine whether the search is in a public place (Section 43) or a private building, conveyance or enclosed place (Section 42).

procedure.title: Conduct Personal Search
procedure.description: Where personal search is required, comply with safeguards provided under Section 50.

procedure.title: Search Premises or Vehicle
procedure.description: Conduct systematic search while documenting all recovered narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and related evidence.

procedure.title: Prepare Inventory
procedure.description: Prepare inventory of seized material including description, quantity, packaging, identifying marks and seizure location in accordance with Section 52A.

procedure.title: Photography and Sampling
procedure.description: Photograph seized material and draw representative samples following the NDPS Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal Rules, 2022.

procedure.title: Seal Evidence
procedure.description: Seal all exhibits using tamper-evident methods and assign unique evidence identifiers.

procedure.title: Deposit in Safe Custody
procedure.description: Deposit seized articles in the designated malkhana or authorized storage facility as required under Section 55.

procedure.title: Submit Report
procedure.description: Forward seizure and arrest report to the immediate superior officer within the prescribed time under Section 57.

references: NDPS (Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal) Rules, 2022

data.sop_name: Evidence Collection under the NDPS Act
data.objective: To ensure proper identification, collection, documentation, preservation and transfer of evidence in narcotics investigations while maintaining evidentiary integrity.

legal_basis.purpose: Preparation of inventory, photography and sampling of seized narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
Safe custody of seized narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
Reporting of arrest and seizure.

procedure.title: Secure the Scene
procedure.description: Restrict unauthorized access to prevent contamination, loss or tampering of evidence.

procedure.title: Identify Evidence
procedure.description: Locate narcotic substances, packaging materials, weighing instruments, digital devices, financial records and other relevant evidence.

procedure.title: Photograph Evidence
procedure.description: Photograph all evidence in its original position before collection.

procedure.title: Prepare Inventory
procedure.description: Record description, quantity, packaging, markings and place of recovery as required under Section 52A.

procedure.title: Draw Representative Samples
procedure.description: Draw representative samples in accordance with the NDPS (Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal) Rules, 2022.

procedure.title: Seal and Label
procedure.description: Seal all evidence using tamper-evident seals and assign a unique evidence identification number.

procedure.title: Document Collection
procedure.description: Record the officer collecting the evidence, date, time, location and witness details.

procedure.title: Transfer for Safe Custody
procedure.description: Transfer evidence to the designated evidence storage facility while maintaining chain of custody.

procedure.title: Forward Samples
procedure.description: Send representative samples to an authorized forensic laboratory with appropriate documentation.

officer_precautions: Do not mix evidence from different seizure locations.
references: NDPS (Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal) Rules, 2022

data.sop_name: Chain of Custody under the NDPS Act
data.objective: To maintain the integrity, authenticity and traceability of seized narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and associated evidence from the time of seizure until final disposal or production before the Court.

legal_basis.purpose: Preparation of inventory, photography, sampling and certification of seized narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
Safe custody of seized narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances and related articles.
Reporting of arrest and seizure to superior officers.

procedure.title: Assign Evidence Identification
procedure.description: Assign a unique identification number to every seized exhibit immediately after seizure.

procedure.title: Document Evidence
procedure.description: Record description, quantity, packaging, identifying marks, seizure location, date, time and seizing officer.

procedure.title: Seal Evidence
procedure.description: Seal every exhibit using tamper-evident seals and record the seal impression in official documentation.

procedure.title: Prepare Inventory
procedure.description: Prepare inventory and photographic documentation in accordance with Section 52A of the NDPS Act.

procedure.title: Transfer to Safe Custody
procedure.description: Deposit seized material in the designated malkhana or authorized storage facility without unnecessary delay.

procedure.title: Record Every Transfer
procedure.description: Document every transfer of custody including officer names, designation, date, time, purpose and signatures.

procedure.title: Forward Samples
procedure.description: Forward representative samples to an authorized forensic laboratory with proper forwarding documents and seal verification.

procedure.title: Produce Before Court
procedure.description: Produce evidence before the competent Court whenever required while maintaining complete custody records.

procedure.title: Final Disposal
procedure.description: Dispose of seized narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in accordance with judicial orders and applicable NDPS Rules.

officer_responsibilities: Verify seal integrity during every transfer.
Immediately report damaged or broken seals.
Ensure evidence remains secure until final disposal.
references: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
NDPS (Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal) Rules, 2022
Directorate of Forensic Science Services Guidelines

data.sop_name: Arrest Procedure under the NDPS Act
data.objective: To ensure lawful arrest, documentation and production of accused persons in accordance with the NDPS Act, 1985 and the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).

legal_basis.purpose: Power to issue warrants and authorizations for arrest.
Power to arrest based on prior information in specified places.
Power to arrest in public places.
Procedure after arrest.
Mandatory report of arrest and seizure.

procedure.title: Establish Legal Grounds
procedure.description: Confirm that reasonable grounds exist for arrest under the NDPS Act.

procedure.title: Identify the Officer
procedure.description: The arresting officer shall identify themselves and disclose their authority.

procedure.title: Inform the Accused
procedure.description: Inform the accused of the grounds of arrest and applicable provisions of law.

procedure.title: Conduct Personal Search
procedure.description: Where applicable, conduct personal search in accordance with Section 50 of the NDPS Act.

procedure.title: Prepare Arrest Memo
procedure.description: Prepare an arrest memo containing the date, time, location, witnesses and signatures.

procedure.title: Seize Relevant Evidence
procedure.description: Secure narcotic substances, digital devices, documents and other material connected to the offence.

procedure.title: Medical Examination
procedure.description: Arrange medical examination whenever required under applicable law.

procedure.title: Produce Before Magistrate
procedure.description: Produce the arrested person before the competent Magistrate within the legally prescribed period.

procedure.title: Submit Report
procedure.description: Forward arrest and seizure report to the immediate superior officer in accordance with Section 57.

rights_of_accused: To be informed of the grounds of arrest.
To be produced before a Magistrate within the prescribed legal period.
To consult a legal practitioner as permitted by law.
To receive a copy of the arrest memo.

data.objective: Provide structured knowledge regarding common trafficking route characteristics observed in narcotics investigations to support intelligence analysis, investigation planning and machine learning feature interpretation.

route_patterns.description: Movement of narcotic drugs across one or more state boundaries using road, rail, air or courier networks.
Distribution occurring within a single state through regional transportation networks.

risk_indicators: Repeated use of commercial transport services.
Movement inconsistent with declared occupation or purpose.
Use of multiple transport modes during a single journey.
investigation_guidelines: Verify travel history.
Compare origin and destination with intelligence records.
Coordinate with relevant enforcement agencies when multiple jurisdictions are involved.
Review transport and booking documentation.
Document movement chronology during investigation.
references: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) World Drug Report

data.objective: Provide operational intelligence regarding common transportation methods, vehicle usage and movement patterns observed in narcotics trafficking investigations to support risk assessment and investigation planning.

transport_patterns.common_usage: Most frequently used for interstate distribution due to extensive highway connectivity and operational flexibility.
Used for transporting concealed narcotics over long distances through passenger or parcel services.
Primarily associated with international trafficking, courier networks and passenger baggage concealment.
Increasingly used for concealed shipments through commercial logistics services.

route_characteristics.description: Movement of narcotic substances across state boundaries requiring coordination between enforcement agencies.
Distribution occurring within a single state through local transportation networks.

investigation_indicators: Repeated movement along known trafficking corridors.
Use of hired or borrowed vehicles.
Frequent courier bookings under different identities.
investigation_guidelines: Verify ownership of the vehicle.
Examine travel history and route consistency.
Coordinate with neighboring state agencies for interstate cases.
Inspect hidden compartments and modified vehicle structures.
Review transport documentation where applicable.
references: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) World Drug Report

data.objective: Provide structured intelligence regarding commonly encountered concealment methods in narcotics investigations to support evidence identification, investigative analysis and machine learning feature interpretation.

concealment_patterns.description: Hidden compartments incorporated into luggage or baggage for concealing narcotic substances.
Modified compartments within vehicles identified during enforcement operations.
Commercial courier consignments intercepted during enforcement or customs inspections.
Commercial food packages identified during seizure operations.
Personal care or cosmetic containers examined during baggage or parcel inspections.
Concealment within garments or personal belongings identified during lawful searches.

investigation_guidelines: Photograph concealed evidence before recovery whenever practicable.
Document the concealment location in detail.
Maintain chain of custody throughout recovery.
Collect fingerprints or DNA where appropriate.
Record concealment method for intelligence analysis.
references: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) World Drug Report

data.objective: Provide structured knowledge regarding intelligence sources commonly used during narcotics investigations to support intelligence analysis, investigation planning and machine learning feature interpretation.

intelligence_sources.description: Information received from confidential human sources assisting law enforcement agencies.
Information obtained through lawful physical or electronic surveillance during investigations.
Operational intelligence developed or shared by the Narcotics Control Bureau.
Information generated by State Police Special Branches and Anti-Narcotics Units.
Information exchanged between law enforcement agencies operating across multiple jurisdictions.
Information voluntarily provided by members of the public requiring independent verification.
Information derived from lawful analysis of digital platforms, online communications and cyber investigations.

verification_principles: Corroborate intelligence using independent sources wherever possible.
Document the origin of every intelligence input.
Record intelligence handling in accordance with agency procedures.
